content.value_statement: Drug discovery teams need reliable access to compound, target, and bioactivity records. This skill guides focused ChEMBL queries, structure searches, and result interpretation.
actual_capabilities: Search molecules by ChEMBL ID, preferred name, or physicochemical property filters.
Retrieve target details and search single-protein targets by name.
Filter activity records by target, compound, measurement type, potency, and units.
Run similarity and substructure searches from SMILES inputs.
Retrieve drug records, mechanisms, indications, and compound activity histories.
Convert returned records into pandas DataFrames and apply caching or pagination guidance.
limitations: Queries require the ChEMBL Python client, network access, and availability of the public ChEMBL service.
The skill does not provide an offline database snapshot or a bulk-download pipeline.
Examples do not validate SMILES, normalize mixed units, deduplicate records, or perform statistical SAR modeling.
ChEMBL records can contain inconsistent or duplicate measurements and must not be treated as clinical advice.

use_cases.title: Prioritize target inhibitors
use_cases.description: Find compounds below a chosen potency threshold and retain assay context, units, and validity flags.

use_cases.title: Map compound-target evidence
use_cases.description: Retrieve compound activities, mechanisms, and indications to examine target relationships or repurposing hypotheses.

use_cases.title: Build analysis tables
use_cases.description: Filter ChEMBL records and convert results into DataFrames for quality review and downstream analysis.

prompt_templates.title: Profile a known compound
prompt_templates.prompt: Find ChEMBL information for aspirin or CHEMBL25. Summarize identifiers, molecular properties, mechanisms, indications, and available bioactivity records.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner lookup for a known molecule

prompt_templates.title: Find potent target compounds
prompt_templates.prompt: Find IC50 records for EGFR target CHEMBL203 at or below 100 nM. Include compound IDs, values, units, assays, and validity flags.
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused potency screening for a defined target

prompt_templates.title: Explore a structure series
prompt_templates.prompt: Search ChEMBL for molecules at least 80 percent similar to this SMILES: [SMILES]. Compare molecular properties and activity records for target [CHEMBL ID].

prompt_templates.title: Design a quality-controlled SAR review
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a reproducible ChEMBL review for target [CHEMBL ID]. Apply activity, unit, property, and similarity filters. Flag duplicates, validity comments, missing values, and assay differences.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced comparative analysis with data-quality controls

output: Profile: preferred name, formula, molecular properties, structure identifiers, drug mechanisms, indications, and available activities.
Quality note: review data validity and source fields before downstream use.

output_examples.input: Find EGFR inhibitors with IC50 values at or below 100 nM.
output: Filter: IC50 at or below 100 nM, with standard units fixed to nM.
Result columns: compound ID, activity value, assay details, pChEMBL value, validity comment, and duplicate flag.

output_examples.input: Compare compounds similar to a query SMILES for a SAR review.
output: Similarity set: compounds meeting the requested threshold.
Comparison: structure identifiers, molecular properties, target activities, units, and assay context.
Review notes: mixed measurements, missing values, duplicate records, and unsupported conclusions are identified.

best_practices: Use stable ChEMBL identifiers after confirming fuzzy name-search results.
Keep measurement type, value, units, assay context, validity comments, and duplicate flags together.
Use caching, pagination, and narrow filters to reduce repeated requests and respect fair usage.
anti_patterns: Do not compare activity values across mixed units or measurement types without normalization.
Do not treat the first fuzzy target match as authoritative without checking its identifier and organism.
Do not interpret a database hit as validated efficacy, safety, or clinical suitability.

faq.question: Does this skill require a ChEMBL API key?
faq.answer: No API key is described for public ChEMBL access. The Python client and network access are required.

faq.question: Can it search by molecular structure?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents similarity and substructure searches using SMILES strings and configurable similarity thresholds.

faq.question: Which bioactivity measurements can it retrieve?
faq.answer: It can filter available ChEMBL activities such as IC50, Ki, Kd, and EC50, with values and units.

faq.question: Can results be exported for analysis?
faq.answer: Yes. Returned records can be converted into a pandas DataFrame when pandas is installed.

faq.question: Does the skill guarantee clean and comparable data?
faq.answer: No. Users must review units, assay context, validity comments, duplicates, and missing values before comparison.

faq.question: Is this suitable for clinical decisions?
faq.answer: No. ChEMBL records support research and hypothesis generation, not medical diagnosis, treatment, or clinical validation.
